t: Causal Relationship Analyzer: a plain-language overview
title: Causal Relationship Analyzer: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Causal Relationship Analyzer does and why archives need it. A causal relationship analyzer reads claims about cause and effect and sorts them honestly: did the text prove a cause, show a mere correlation, or just guess? 'Smoking causes cancer' (asserted cause), 'ice cream sales track drownings' (correlation), 'maybe the policy helped' (hypothesis) — each gets its proper label. The archive stops mistaking coincidence for proof.
demo:
# Causal Relationship Analyzer - runnable demo (JAH-ATK169-000001)
import re
RANK = 1
SIG = False
CLAIMS = ['The drought led to crop failures.', 'Ice cream sales track drowning rates.', 'The policy may have helped growth.', 'Smoking caused by advertising? No — smoking is correlated with stress.']
CAUSE = ["caused by", "led to", "resulted in", "produced", "triggered"]
CORR = ["correlated with", "associated with", "tracks", "linked to"]
HEDGE = ["may", "might", "suggests", "could", "possibly", "hypothesis"]
def classify(c):
    cl = c.lower()
    if any(h in cl for h in HEDGE): return "hypothesis"
    if any(w in cl for w in CAUSE): return "asserted cause"
    if any(w in cl for w in CORR): return "correlation"
    return "no causal claim"
for c in CLAIMS:
    print("[%-15s] %s" % (classify(c), c[:65]))
if RANK >= 2:
    from collections import Counter
    print("class histogram:", dict(Counter(classify(c) for c in CLAIMS)))
if RANK >= 3:
    risky = [c for c in CLAIMS if classify(c) == "asserted cause"]
    print("claims needing evidence review:", len(risky))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-CAU-" + "JAH-ATK169-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK169-000001", "OK")

t: How the Causal Relationship Analyzer works: the deep tour
title: How the Causal Relationship Analyzer works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Causal Relationship Analyzer does and why archives need it. Real analyzers classify causal language with cue lexicons — 'caused by', 'led to', 'resulted in' mark asserted causation; 'associated with', 'correlated with' mark correlation; hedges like 'may', 'suggests', 'could explain' mark hypotheses. Stronger systems check for causal-study designs (randomized trials, instrumental variables, Granger causality tests in time series) and flag reverse-causation risks. Each claim is labeled with its evidence class and the exact cue or design that earned the label. Advanced analysis applies causal-graph checks (confounders, colliders, mediators) to statistical claims and requires temporal precedence — a cause must precede its effect — as a hard filter. Quality is measured by classification accuracy on annotated claim corpora and by false-cause rate: how often the system upgrades correlation to causation. The limits are genuine scientific uncertainty and adversarial framing; the analyzer reports its evidence class and never upgrades a hedge into a fact, because the upgrade is where misinformation starts.

description: Production: how the Causal Relationship Analyzer runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real analyzers classify causal language with cue lexicons — 'caused by', 'led to', 'resulted in' mark asserted causation; 'associated with', 'correlated with' mark correlation; hedges like 'may', 'suggests', 'could explain' mark hypotheses. Stronger systems check for causal-study designs (randomized trials, instrumental variables, Granger causality tests in time series) and flag reverse-causation risks. Each claim is labeled with its evidence class and the exact cue or design that earned the label.
demo:
# Causal Relationship Analyzer - runnable demo (JAH-ATK169-000014)
import re
RANK = 2
SIG = False
CLAIMS = ['The outage was triggered by a faulty relay.', 'Exercise is associated with longevity.', 'This might explain the anomaly.']
CAUSE = ["caused by", "led to", "resulted in", "produced", "triggered"]
CORR = ["correlated with", "associated with", "tracks", "linked to"]
HEDGE = ["may", "might", "suggests", "could", "possibly", "hypothesis"]
def classify(c):
    cl = c.lower()
    if any(h in cl for h in HEDGE): return "hypothesis"
    if any(w in cl for w in CAUSE): return "asserted cause"
    if any(w in cl for w in CORR): return "correlation"
    return "no causal claim"
for c in CLAIMS:
    print("[%-15s] %s" % (classify(c), c[:65]))
if RANK >= 2:
    from collections import Counter
    print("class histogram:", dict(Counter(classify(c) for c in CLAIMS)))
if RANK >= 3:
    risky = [c for c in CLAIMS if classify(c) == "asserted cause"]
    print("claims needing evidence review:", len(risky))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-CAU-" + "JAH-ATK169-000014")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK169-000014", "OK")

t: The Causal Relationship Analyzer at archive scale
title: The Causal Relationship Analyzer at archive scale
description: Production: how the Causal Relationship Analyzer runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real analyzers classify causal language with cue lexicons — 'caused by', 'led to', 'resulted in' mark asserted causation; 'associated with', 'correlated with' mark correlation; hedges like 'may', 'suggests', 'could explain' mark hypotheses. Stronger systems check for causal-study designs (randomized trials, instrumental variables, Granger causality tests in time series) and flag reverse-causation risks. Each claim is labeled with its evidence class and the exact cue or design that earned the label. Advanced analysis applies causal-graph checks (confounders, colliders, mediators) to statistical claims and requires temporal precedence — a cause must precede its effect — as a hard filter. Quality is measured by classification accuracy on annotated claim corpora and by false-cause rate: how often the system upgrades correlation to causation. The limits are genuine scientific uncertainty and adversarial framing; the analyzer reports its evidence class and never upgrades a hedge into a fact, because the upgrade is where misinformation starts.
